_readme: Tunables for the escalation ladder. Every value carries its provenance.
MEASURED = derived from a run on this machine. PROVISIONAL = starting point,
replace with the output of scripts/ladder-calibrate.mjs before trusting it.
Edit this file, not the hook sources.
_minChars: MEASURED 2026-08-09 on this machine: ladder-calibrate.mjs against
/Users/rob/Development/squeez gave a median rung-2 reduction of 56.9% and
200 / (0.569 * 0.318) = 1105 -> 1100. Caveat: that clone carries a single
commit, so the git samples are thin; ls -laR (67.3%) and du -a (90.2%)
carried the median. Re-run against a repo with real history before treating
this as settled. Original rationale follows.
Idee 1. Below this many characters of stashed original, skip
rung 2 and let squeez_retrieve through untouched. Rationale: rung 2 costs a
re-execution (wall clock, and a determinism risk) to save a fraction of a
small number. At 1000 chars the whole original is ~318 tokens (measured
ratio, see _tokensPerKilochar); rtk would save ~40% of that = ~130 tokens.
RUN scripts/ladder-calibrate.mjs ON YOUR OWN CORPUS BEFORE FIXING THIS.
_tokensPerKilochar: MEASURED on 19 real command outputs (express + requests repos) with
tiktoken o200k_base: 318 tok/1000 chars mean, range 230-479.
Dense tabular output (ps aux, ls -la) sits at ~479; prose-like at ~230.
chars/4 (what rtk and squeez both use internally) yields 250 and therefore
UNDERCOUNTS by ~27% on this corpus. bash-size-feedback.mjs uses /3 = 333,
which is close and slightly conservative — keep it.
_maxRedirectsPerSession: Over-instruction is the measured failure mode on this machine (3.5k tokens
of SessionStart guidance -> 0 of 92 ctx calls, session 7221ee3f). Same
_noSqueezPrefix: UNVERIFIED — prepended to the suggested rung-2 command so squeez's own
PreToolUse hook does not re-wrap it. Without this, rung-2 output is fed
back through squeez, where cross-call dedup can collapse it against the
very stash we are escaping ('identical to <hash> at bash#N') and the
handler dispatch sees 'rtk' instead of the real command.
VERIFY on the live install: run a bash call prefixed with --no-squeez and
confirm no '# squeez [...]' header appears. If the prefix is not honoured,
set this to "" and accept the double-compression risk, or drop rung 2.
_deterministicHeads: Rung 2 RE-RUNS the command; it does not read the stash. For anything whose
output moves between two executions the re-run returns FRESH data while the
model believes it received the original. That is a correctness trap, not a
token question — so redirection is allowlist-only.
Deliberately absent: ps, top, date, uptime, curl, wget, docker logs, kubectl
'git' is included because git object reads are content-addressed; note that
'git status' still depends on the working tree — see workingTreeSensitive.
_workingTreeSensitive: Deterministic only while nothing edits the tree between R1 and R2. The gate
treats these as non-deterministic when any Write/Edit happened in the
session after the stash was recorded (the ledger stamps a write counter).
_rung2: MEASURED rung-2 yields vs verbatim (tiktoken o200k_base):
cat lib/response.js   6574 -> 5976 (rtk read -l minimal,    100% entity recall)
cat lib/response.js   6574 ->  167 (rtk read -l aggressive,  signature mode)
'rtk read -l aggressive' is the strongest rung 2 for source files (keeps
function signatures, replaces bodies with '// ... implementation') but is
wrong when the model needs the body. Kept OUT of the default map on
purpose; suggest it in the reason text instead and let the model choose.
_rung2Filter: ladder-retrieve-filter.mjs — rung 2 as the design conversation meant it:
the RETRIEVED blob is compressed on its way back, instead of the model being
sent off to re-run the command (which is what ladder-retrieve-gate.mjs does
and what cost +9.6% in the 2026-08-09 A/B).
minChars 4000: below that the rtk process spawn costs more than it saves.
maxRatio 0.6: rtk is a no-op on output it has no language filter for (a
maxRatio 0.85: rtk is a no-op on output it has no language filter for (a
git-log dump came back 17120 -> 17119 chars, ratio 0.9999), so the guard only
has to exclude that. Real source lands at 0.05; a dense signature-heavy file
at 0.74. 0.6 would have thrown the latter away for no reason.
_enabled: OFF as of 2026-08-09 — the decision from wave 02-1, taken on the paired A/B.
Frozen corpus, 3 runs per arm, all six dispatched the same way:
arm A (gate off) fresh input 149798 / 158940 / 203879  -> median 158940
arm B (gate on)  fresh input 168540 / 174169 / 191404  -> median 174169
paired delta +9.6% fresh input, +10.2% output, quality identical
(all six reports independently arrived at the same 305 files)
The gate did fire — 2 redirects over 16 stashes — so this is not a coverage
artefact. It fired and cost more: a redirect buys an extra turn, the rung-2
command, and its output, and the model still needed the verbatim original
often enough to eat the saving. The spread inside arm A (36%) is wider than
the delta, so the honest reading is 'no benefit', not 'measurably worse'.
Set true to re-enable without unwiring the hooks — also what the B arm of
_rung2Mode: OFF as of 2026-08-09. Both hook-based rungs are superseded by the `ladder`
command (~/.local/bin/ladder), which reads the stash straight from
~/.claude/squeez/blobs/<key> and runs rtk over it. No MCP round trip, no
deny, no re-execution — so none of the failure modes that made the hooks
unmeasurable apply. Set to "gate" or "filter" to re-enable a hook rung.
The PostToolUse ledger stays wired: `ladder` reads it to recover the file
extension, which is what lets rtk pick a language filter at all.
